once-in-royal-davids-city.sources: // Sources: the song file (the parts' guide notes, as reviewed 2026-11-18), tools: ~/Code/arranger-keep/partfacts.py; licence.source: Hymns Ancient and Modern, with Appendix (London: W. Clowes and Sons, 1868), No. 361, Gauntlett's tune Irby and his four parts, lower parts revoiced; verses 1, 2 and 6; G major

parts.soprano: Carries Gauntlett's tune, Irby, most often on G, then D and B, up to its top E only on the first two syllables of each verse's last two lines ("Mary" and "Jesus" in verse 1, "With the" and "Lived on" in verse 2, "When like" and "All in" in verse 6), and down to its low D only on the first word of each verse's first and third lines ("Once" and "Where", "He" and "And", "Not" and "We").
parts.alto: Sings the words under the tune, most often on B, then D and F-sharp, up to its top G only at the same places in every verse: the fourth syllable of the second and fourth lines (the "ly" of "lowly" and the "ger" of "manger" in verse 1, "and" and the "dle" of "cradle" in verse 2, the "en" of "oxen" and "right" in verse 6), the last word of the fifth line ("mild,", "lowly," and "crowned") and the first, second and fourth syllables of the last line ("Jesus" and "her", "Lived on" and "our", "All in" and "shall"); and down to its low B on many notes, among them the first word of each verse's first four lines.
parts.tenor: Sings the words in the middle of the chord, most often on B and G, then C, up to its top D only on the fourth syllable of each verse's second, fourth and last lines (the "ly" of "lowly", the "ger" of "manger" and "her" in verse 1, "and", the "dle" of "cradle" and "our" in verse 2, the "en" of "oxen", "right" and "shall" in verse 6), and down to its low D only on the sixth syllable of each verse's fifth line (the "ther" of "mother", the "and" of "mean, and lowly" and the "dren" of "children").
parts.bass: Sings the bass line, most often on D, then G, A and B, up to its top G only on the last syllable of each verse's first and third lines (the "ty" of "City" and the "by," of "Baby," in verse 1, the "en" of "heaven" and the "ble," of "stable," in verse 2, then "stable," and "heaven," in verse 6), and down to its low G on the first word of each verse's first and third lines, the third syllable and last word of its fifth line, and the last word of its second, fourth and last lines.

parts_es.soprano: Lleva la melodía de Gauntlett, Irby, con más frecuencia en el Sol, luego en el Re y el Si, sube a su Mi agudo solo en las dos primeras sílabas de los dos últimos versos de cada estrofa ("Mary" y "Jesus" en la estrofa 1, "With the" y "Lived on" en la estrofa 2, "When like" y "All in" en la estrofa 6), y baja a su Re grave solo en la primera palabra del primer y el tercer verso de cada estrofa ("Once" y "Where", "He" y "And", "Not" y "We").
parts_es.alto: Canta la letra por debajo de la melodía, con más frecuencia en el Si, luego en el Re y el Fa sostenido, sube a su Sol agudo solo en los mismos lugares de cada estrofa: la cuarta sílaba del segundo y el cuarto verso (el "ly" de "lowly" y el "ger" de "manger" en la estrofa 1, "and" y el "dle" de "cradle" en la estrofa 2, el "en" de "oxen" y "right" en la estrofa 6), la última palabra del quinto verso ("mild,", "lowly," y "crowned") y la primera, la segunda y la cuarta sílaba del último verso ("Jesus" y "her", "Lived on" y "our", "All in" y "shall"), y baja a su Si grave en muchas notas, entre ellas la primera palabra de los cuatro primeros versos de cada estrofa.
parts_es.tenor: Canta la letra en el centro del acorde, con más frecuencia en el Si y el Sol, luego en el Do, sube a su Re agudo solo en la cuarta sílaba del segundo, el cuarto y el último verso de cada estrofa (el "ly" de "lowly", el "ger" de "manger" y "her" en la estrofa 1, "and", el "dle" de "cradle" y "our" en la estrofa 2, el "en" de "oxen", "right" y "shall" en la estrofa 6), y baja a su Re grave solo en la sexta sílaba del quinto verso de cada estrofa (el "ther" de "mother", el "and" de "mean, and lowly" y el "dren" de "children").
parts_es.bass: Canta la línea del bajo, con más frecuencia en el Re, luego en el Sol, el La y el Si, sube a su Sol agudo solo en la última sílaba del primer y el tercer verso de cada estrofa (el "ty" de "City" y el "by," de "Baby," en la estrofa 1, el "en" de "heaven" y el "ble," de "stable," en la estrofa 2, y luego "stable," y "heaven," en la estrofa 6), y baja a su Sol grave en la primera palabra del primer y el tercer verso de cada estrofa, en la tercera sílaba y la última palabra del quinto verso, y en la última palabra del segundo, el cuarto y el último verso.
